prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor lounge layout where the camera wearer is seated with their own legs, a pink tote bag on the lower left, and a small open case on the lower right all within arm's reach at roughly 0.3 to 0.8 metres. Directly in front of the camera wearer at about 1.5 to 2.0 metres stands a person in a blue jacket and dark trousers facing the camera wearer, while a seated person on the far right is roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres away and about 1.0 metre to the right of the standing person. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's right arm reaches forward and upward in frame 1 (brightest white, ~0.2–0.4 m), tilts downward toward the pink bag in frame 2 as the bag fills the foreground at ~0.3–0.5 metres, rises again in frame 3 while the camera pitches up, and lowers in frames 4 and 5 as the standing person holds a phone slightly closer toward the camera wearer. The depth map clearly separates the foreground reach of the arm and tote bag from the mid-ground standing person and the background coffee table (~2.5 m) and walls (>3.5 m) more distinctly than the cluttered RGB image alone. However, it is unreliable inside the dark interior of the open bag and case where depth flattens, and it loses detail on the background windows and walls which merge into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies the foreground pink tote bag (labeled 'suitcase' or 'backpack') at 0.4 to 0.7 metres on the lower left, the standing person in the center at 1.5 to 2.0 metres, the camera wearer's raised right arm and legs on the lower right within 0.3 to 0.6 metres, and partially visible seated people on the far left and right edges at 1.0 to 2.0 metres. In frame 2, as the camera looks down, the pink bag mask expands to cover the center of the view while the camera wearer's crossed left leg on the left is segmented as a 'person' right next to it (within 0.2 metres of the bag). In frames 3 through 5, the standing person's upper torso (cropped at the top edge, facing forward with head out of view) remains behind the lower-foreground bag and case, while a seated person on the right holds a small object labeled 'remote' within their own arm's reach (~0.3 m from their body) and turns slightly toward the center. Compared to RGB, the segmentation map explicitly isolates overlapping person instances and foreground containers, making the boundary between the standing person's legs and the top rim of the pink bag immediately obvious. However, the map is unreliable in class consistency and completeness: it mislabels the soft pink tote bag and the small drone/device case as 'suitcase' or 'backpack' with overlapping text ('suitcasek'), merges the camera wearer's arm with the seated neighbour on the right in frame 3, and completely misses the standing person's handheld phone in frame 5 as well as the background coffee table.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks the 2D joint and finger positions in the upper-middle and right portions of the scene, highlighting the standing person's torso and arms at 1.5 to 2.0 metres in frames 3 and 4, and the camera wearer's right hand within 0.4 metres in frames 2 and 3. In frame 2, a magenta hand skeleton shows the camera wearer's right fingers gripping the upper right rim of the pink bag, and in frame 3 that same hand is raised in front of the right side of the view while the standing person's yellow torso and upper-arm skeleton appears above and behind the bag, facing directly toward the camera wearer with both hands brought together at chest height (~1.5 m away). In frame 4, the standing person's shoulder-and-torso rectangle and clustered magenta finger joints remain centered at chest level as they hold a phone within their own arm's reach, with their head cropped out above the top edge of the frame. This map reveals exact finger articulation and bilateral shoulder orientation for the standing person and the camera wearer's reaching hand that are partially motion-blurred or visually cluttered against clothing in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is highly sparse and unreliable across the strip, completely failing to detect any skeletons in frames 1 and 5, omitting the standing person's legs in all frames, and missing the seated people on the left and right edges entirely.
